note: Taste is built for company websites. Crewcut is an app: a glass window with a sidebar, a main column and a right column. Checks that only make sense for a landing page are waived here, each with its reason. Every other FAIL must be fixed. Reviewed 17 Nov 2026 against the screens run of the media-first look.

waivers.reason: An app has no hero section; the first screen is the work itself (DESIGN.md rule 2).
An app has no hero section; the first screen is the work itself (DESIGN.md rule 2).
The app is one fixed window, not a page of full-height sections.
The app is one fixed window, not a page of sections.

A landing-page rule (one .wrap container with equal margins on every section). The app is one window with three columns of their own widths and insets (DESIGN.md rules 2 and 7); the composer dock floats centred on its column.
There is no marketing call to action in the app; the one action is the card button (rule 12).
The note 'Demo data. Nothing here is real.' appears only in demo mode and must stay (rule 17: test data only, said so).
Panels and the composer float over the scrolling columns of the window on purpose (DESIGN.md rules 7 and 18); Taste measures the boxes, not what is visible.
Titles and rows stay on one line and truncate; the full text is in the title attribute and the opened view (DESIGN.md rule 5).
The app's type scale is fixed by DESIGN.md rule 5 (20 / 15 / 13 / 12 / 11), not the scale of a landing page.

The flagged change is the elapsed-time clock of a job (one update per second, no animation). Slate's states play once and hold still (working: four ticks of 0.9 s, again only when a new step is reported); the only looping animation is the run shimmer of working jobs (rule 9), which stops with the work.

Cards change colour only on hover (CSS, rule 9: colour and opacity, no transform); the movement Taste measured comes from live content in the same scene (clocks, the run shimmer). Re-check on the next release.
The composer draws its focus ring around the whole capsule with :focus-within (rule 15), not on the inner textarea.
The composer has a visually hidden label ('Message') linked with for/id and a placeholder that says what to do (rule 3: the only field of the app).
A chat holds several cards, each a labelled group with its own h2 title under the episode's h1; one heading per section is a landing-page rule.
A landing-page rule (each section one screen tall). The home is one scrolling column of an app window: its sections are as tall as their pictures (DESIGN.md rules 2 and 7).
A landing-page copy rule (a hard fact from the brief on the first screen). The app's first screen is the work itself: the counts sit in the pills, the lengths on the pictures, the money in Spend.
